model_name: GEO combined: V4.1-A for dialect, v3.1 for gender and age

model_card.caption: Test results of the models this app uses, scored the way the app scores a recording
rows: RBVD: the nine original voices, unseen sentences
RegSpeech12: speakers never heard in training (5 districts)
BanglaAccent: new speakers reading standard Bangla (another corpus)
model_card.description: Two trained copies of the same network work together. Each reads the log-mel spectrogram (ResNet-50) and the MFCC sequence (two-layer Bi-LSTM) of every 5-second window. The dialect answer comes from GEO V4.1-A, which learned dialect from RBVD (8 districts) and RegSpeech12 (Chattogram, Barishal, Rangpur, Noakhali, Tangail). Gender and age come from GEO v3.1, which learned them from Mozilla Common Voice Bangla. No gender or age label was taken from RBVD.

limits.title: Dialect: Chattogram, Barishal, Rangpur, Noakhali, Tangail
limits.text: Learned from many speakers. On RegSpeech12 speakers it never heard, 73.1% of clips were right (Rangpur 93%, Chottogram 74%, Barishal 63%, Tangail 60%). Read speech in standard Bangla is much harder: 9.3% on BanglaAccent.

limits.title: Dialect: Mymensingh, Jamalpur, Natore
limits.text: Still learned from one RBVD speaker each, so answers for new speakers from these districts are not reliable.

limits.title: Gender and age group
limits.text: Gender was right for 93.3% of Common Voice speakers it never heard. Age has two groups (under 30, 30+) because Common Voice Bangla has no labelled speakers aged 60 or over; its balanced accuracy is 0.61, so treat it as a rough guess.

report.note: The combination was chosen after the V4.1 results were seen; each part's numbers were measured on the same test clips before that choice.
